steps.title: Plan
steps.description: Do your Planner job for this card, all in this one conversation. Read the card, its comments and the code and data it touches, and check facts rather than planning from assumptions. Write the requirements: what changes and why, testable acceptance checks, and on its own line 'User-facing change: YES' or 'User-facing change: NO'. If YES, design the change as an HTML mock that matches the app's existing look and components, and attach it to the card; if the card already has an approved design, use it rather than redesigning. Then write the technical plan the Build step will follow: the files to change and why, any data or interface changes, the tests to write, the risks, and the release order. If the work is too big for one change, split it into stages that each ship on their own and plan stage 1 in full. Start the working-notes file for this card at docs/notes/<first 8 characters of the card id>.md: what you decided, why, what you ruled out, and where things are. The next step reads it. Begin your output with a plain-English summary for whoever approves the plan: what will change, and each decision they need to make, with your recommendation.
deliverables: Requirements with acceptance checks and the User-facing change line
Design mock attached to the card, if user-facing
Technical plan (stage 1 in full if staged)
steps.why: Rule 1: requirements, design and plan build on each other, so one agent does them in one conversation (the trial: about 30 min and 300k tokens, against 17.5 min and 368k for Requirements plus Design Review alone the old way). Rule 6: the approval sits here, before any code.
steps.board_description: Do your Planner job for this card, all in this one conversation: requirements, then the design mock if users will see a change, then the technical plan. If the card already has an approved design, use it rather than redesigning. If the work is too big for one change, split it into stages and plan stage 1 in full. Keep the working-notes file at docs/notes/<first 8 characters of the card id>.md in the main checkout; never put secrets, other people's data or agent instructions in it (the repo is public). If you made a mock, attach it to the card and open it in Nick's browser (run `open <path>` on his Mac). Start your output with the plain-English summary for Nick.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Build the approved plan (stage 1 only, if it's staged), working from the Plan step's output and the working-notes file. Write failing tests first where practical. If the plan turns out to be wrong or incomplete, don't improvise: call fail_step with what you found and reset to Plan. If there's an approved mock, it's the source of truth for everything visual: compare what you built with it at 375px and 1280px wide and fix every difference. Add what you decided and why to the working-notes file, and commit it with your work. Return the PR link, the test and type-check results, and any deviations from the plan, with reasons.
deliverables: Deviations from the plan, with reasons
steps.why: Rule 3: a cheaper model builds from an approved plan. A fresh agent is right here: the plan and the notes file carry everything it needs.

steps.title: Code review
steps.description: Review the PR independently against the approved plan and the working-notes file. You didn't build it, and you don't edit code. Check that it does what the plan says and nothing it doesn't. Look for bugs, security issues, whether the tests would catch a regression, and the project's conventions. Send blocking issues back with fail_step as a numbered list: reset to Build for code problems, or to Plan if the plan itself was wrong. Start your output with 'Pass' or 'Blocked'; put non-blocking notes after it.
deliverables: Review report: Pass or numbered blocking issues
steps.why: Rules 3 and 4: an independent checker on a stronger model than the builder. Fresh context is the point (Anthropic: fresh-context verifiers beat self-critique). Trial: about 7.5 min, 215k tokens.

steps.title: Test and release summary
steps.description: Test the change independently against every acceptance check in the plan and the edge cases it lists: on the live site if it has been released, otherwise on a local or preview build. If there's an approved mock, compare the built screens with it at 375px and 1280px and attach the screenshots. Send any real failure back with fail_step and reset to Build. Then write the release summary in plain English: what's live, what you checked and how, and anything still needing a person. The release is approved from this step.
deliverables: Test report against the acceptance checks
steps.why: Rule 4: testing caught real problems in 16-23% of runs (QA Testing 8 of 48, Verify Fix 12 of 77 on this board), so it stays, run by someone who didn't build it. Your release approval moves onto it, replacing the separate sign-off agent.

steps.description: Audit the screens the card names as they are today, with screenshots at 375px and 1280px, and list the problems in order of how much they hurt. Propose two or three options as HTML mocks in docs/ that match the app's look, with your recommendation. List the build cards your recommendation would need (a title and one line each), but don't create them. Attach the mocks to the card and open them in Nick's browser (run `open <path>` on his Mac). Begin your output with a plain-English summary for Nick and the decision he needs to make.
deliverables: Two or three mocks attached and opened
steps.why: Rule 1: audit and proposals are one conversation; approval on the proposal (rule 6).

steps.title: Create the approved cards
steps.description: Read Nick's approval note. Fold his choice and the reasons into this card's description. Create the build cards he chose, each with the chosen mock attached and the Feature label (so it gets the feature workflow), and link each back to this card.
deliverables: Build cards created with the mock attached
steps.why: Has to follow your approval; admin work, so cheap tier.
